MOTION DESIGN INSTRUCTIONS (YOUTUBE SHORTS - around 150 to 180 seconds long)

- Cover the full timeline of the video with Dan Koe–style motion graphics. Entire length of Video must be covered with no blanks

- Plan around 13 to 15 segments of roughly ~ 16 seconds each. Each segment renders a graphic with changing visuals and multiple text reveals.

- 'front load more aggressive infographics to engage the viewer right up front' or 'use bold Koe style shapes in the first 10 seconds').

- Assume background video is a blank black glossy screen - so you must keep persistent visuals (animation or text) through out the segments and segments must merge into each other like a relay race.

--------------------------------------------------
PACING & ANIMATION RULES
--------------------------------------------------
- No static holds beyond 6 seconds. Introduce visual changes every 2–4 seconds.
- Use only basic transforms: opacity, position, scale. Keep animations single-property per element.
- Prefer step-based reveals over continuous motion. Avoid preset/template animations.
- No gaps in infographic coverage. No dependency on external assets.
mosaic_default_prompt:
MOTION DESIGN INSTRUCTIONS (YOUTUBE SHORTS - 150 to 180 seconds long)

ROLE & OBJECTIVE:
- Generate continuous, minimalist Dan Koe / Vox-style conceptual infographics and blueprint visual models across the entire timeline.
- Pure black background (#000000). The entire video must be visually covered with zero blank moments.
- Plan 13 to 15 continuous segments (~16 seconds each) that flow seamlessly into one another like a relay race.

CRITICAL TEXT & SUBTITLE RULES:
- STRICTLY NO SPOKEN DIALOGUE TEXT, NO SUBTITLE SENTENCES, NO TRANSCRIPT QUOTE CARDS.
- Dialogue captions are handled automatically by a separate Cinematic Captions layer.
- Motion graphics must focus 100% on diagrammatic and conceptual visuals: flowcharts, relational nodes, concentric radar rings, comparison metrics, progress meters, conceptual icons, and abstract geometry.
- If labeling is required for diagrams, use only concise 1-2 word node labels (e.g., "Input", "Output", "Signal", "Noise"). Never print spoken sentences.

VISUAL STRUCTURE & HOOK:
- Hook: Front-load bold, aggressive blueprint geometry in the first 5-10 seconds to immediately hook viewer retention.
- Relay Race Transitions: When one diagram concludes, morph or transition smoothly into the next conceptual model without hard black cuts.

PACING & CONSERVATIVE RENDERING RULES (MANDATORY FOR EXPORT STABILITY):
- Introduce subtle visual changes or step reveals every 2 to 4 seconds. No static holds beyond 5 seconds.
- Lightweight transforms only: opacity, position, scale. Keep animations strictly single-property per element.
- Prefer discrete step-based reveals over complex physics, particle engines, or 3D meshes to ensure fast, reliable rendering without timeouts.
- Zero external asset dependencies: all shapes, icons, and diagrams must be natively drawn vector/CSS geometry.
